seo_title: Coca-Cola Case Study: Foodie Creator Whitespace | SOMIN
description: SOMIN read Foodie creators and the cola category for Coca-Cola in four markets and found home cooking at 62.9% of Indian creator content, with cola at 0%.
eyebrow: Brand case study · Soft drinks · 4 markets
h1: Coca-Cola owns the table in 4 markets, Foodie creators own the kitchen
lede: SOMIN read Coca-Cola, 2–5 soft-drink rivals and 5–7 Foodie creators in each of India, the UK, Mexico and South Africa. Creators were loudest on home cooking and regional discovery, up to 82.9% of their content; cola had 0%.
meta_line: A SOMIN brand briefing · Jun 2025 – May 2026 · India, United Kingdom, Mexico, South Africa · Foodies

stats.label: Indian Foodie-creator voice on home cooking

challenge.title: Coca-Cola's voice sits in celebration and sport, like its rivals
challenge.body: Benchmarking Pepsi, Limca, Corona or Irn-Bru only shows where parity is required. The question was where Foodie audiences talk, and whether cola is there at all.

approach.title: Three cohorts and eight content strands in each of 4 markets
points: Perspective Studies on Coca-Cola, competitors and leading Foodie creators over four quarters.
Share of voice across eight content strands, from home cooking to sports fandom.
One anchor SOMIN persona and three pillars per market.
Share and volume read together, so a falling share is not mistaken for decline.

findings_title: Home cooking and regional discovery are open in all 4 markets

findings.title: Home cooking is 62.9% of Indian Foodie content, cola 0%
findings.body: Coca-Cola and its rivals had 0.0%; Coca-Cola put 57.1% of its voice into shared celebration.

findings.title: Regional discovery: 76.8% in Mexico, 82.9% in South Africa
findings.body: Authentic and regional culinary discovery, where neither Coca-Cola nor its rivals published.

findings.title: UK creators split 48.2% home cooking, 43.7% discovery
findings.body: Cola sat at 0.0% on both; Coca-Cola put 69.2% of its voice into shared celebration.

delivered.title: A persona and three pillars for each of Coca-Cola's 4 markets
points: Pillars such as Home-Cooking Confidence, World on Your Table, Reclaim the Roots and Honour the Craft
A whitespace table and quarterly topicality read per market
Strategic angles mapped per tension, one to pick per pillar
A cross-market plan: lead with culinary whitespace, hold an everyday-pairing bridge, defend or extend the third pillar

quote.text: Coca-Cola owns the table. The Foodie creators own the kitchen.

outcome.title: Coca-Cola should lead each market on its culinary whitespace
outcome.body: Creator collaborations lead on home cooking or authentic discovery, SOMIN moments set the calendar, the everyday-pairing bridge runs on real propositions, and celebration is defended in Mexico and South Africa.

faq.q: Why look at Foodie creators and not only at competitors?
faq.a: Competitors show only the floor. Foodie creators spot food trends first, so where their audience leans in and no cola brand follows is the opportunity.

faq.q: What does whitespace mean in this briefing?
faq.a: Whitespace: the creator cohort, a proxy for demand, is active and the cola category is not. A quiet brand alone does not count; its silence may be deliberate.

faq.q: Is the plan the same in every market?
faq.a: The move is the same: lead with culinary whitespace and keep an everyday-pairing bridge where Coca-Cola has a foothold. The persona, pillars and cultural route change.

faq.q: Why read volume as well as share?
faq.a: In India, creator share on regional discovery fell from 81% to 37%, but volume grew from 48 to 559 posts: a composition effect, not a decline.
